Thanks, Olga — quick note from our side before the kickoff:

We ran a two-week sampling of production traffic and attached a small slice (prod-traffic-samples.csv). Our high-level goals: 1) reduce per-token cost by ~35–45%; 2) keep p95 latency below 300ms for our interactive endpoints; 3) avoid any noticeable quality regressions for our customer-facing summarization model.

Main asks for the implementation phase: batching and KV-prefetch parameters that will work with our 99th-percentile peak spikes, a recommended quantization profile we can test in canary, and a routing policy for warm vs. cold tenants. We’d like a week-by-week plan with clear sign-off gates (canary, perf regression check, rollout).

Can you draft a short implementation plan and share the artifacts you’ll need from our side? Lina (cc) is handling procurement and will also need a timeline for procurement/contracting milestones.

Thanks,
Samir
Infrastructure Lead, BrightGrid

From: Olga Petrov <olga@redwood.com>

Subject: Precision inference economics — implementation sync

Thanks for the sample, Samir — this is exactly what we need to shape the plan. I put together a concise mutual-action plan and attached a one-page map plus an initial quant profile spreadsheet. Summary below; please treat times as proposed and we can adjust during the kickoff.

High level approach (proposed):
- Week 0 (Prep): Redwood and BrightGrid exchange key artifacts (traffic samples, model checkpoints, authorization for canary region).
- Week 1 (Profiling): Redwood runs offline profiling against the samples to produce baseline token cost and latency distribution; supply per-endpoint latency/cost matrix.
- Week 2 (Canary): Apply conservative quantization profile + prefix KV caching + adaptive batching in a canary environment (small % of traffic). Monitor output quality via prompt set and perf (p95 target 300ms).
- Week 3 (Iterate): Tighten batch sizes and try alternate quant rigs if quality permits; enable routing policy for warm tenants and automatic fallback to full-precision variants for cold starts.
- Week 4 (Rollout): Gradual ramp with gating on quality and cost metrics; handoff to BrightGrid ops for day-to-day controls.

Key success criteria (must pass to proceed between gates):
- No >2% degradation on the comparator prompt set (quality).
- P95 latency <= 300ms for interactive endpoints during canary.
- Per-token cost reduction >= 35% in canary.

Artifacts we attached for your review: precision-econ-map.pdf (one-page action map), quant-profile-suggestions.xlsx (baseline profiles we intend to try). We’ll also need SSH/agent access for canary logs and a short list of critical prompt queries you care about for quality checks.

Next steps:
- Can we lock a 45-minute kickoff today at 11:00 AM PT? If that works, Marcus will walk the kernel compatibility notes and I’ll present the mutual action plan. Lina — please advise procurement lead contact if timeline looks good.

Thanks,
Olga Petrov
Customer Success Manager — Redwood Inference

Great — a couple of technical clarifications to prep the canary so we’re aligned on trade-offs. A short checklist and recommendations below.

Quick checklist for canary environment:
- Model variant and checkpoint hash (we need the exact commit to ensure kernel selection).
- Target sequence length distribution (we’ll pick batch windows based on common token counts).
- A list of ~20 representative prompts for quality regression tests (we’ll seed these into the eval harness).

Quantization guidance (initial):
- Start with int8 A/B: we’ll run int8-opt and int8-symmetric profiles in parallel in canary. int8-opt generally gives ~30–40% cost reduction with low quality impact for classification and summarization tasks; we’ll fallback to fp16 for any degenerate prompts.
- If int8 fails quality gates, try mixed-precision path (kv-cache preserved as fp16 while compute goes int8) — this often keeps latency improvements while preserving long-context quality.

Batching and KV cache:
- Use adaptive batching with a 20ms aggregation window for interactive endpoints; this balances latency and throughput for BrightGrid’s spike patterns.
- Warm-tenant routing: sticky routing to warmed GPU pools using prefix-based KV prefetch. Cold tenants should default to a lower-batch, lower-quant profile to minimize error risk.

Compatibility note: we found one older kernel in your model family that requires a specific fused-attn kernel; I attached the kernel-compat-matrix.csv with a quick mapping and recommended runtime flags. If you can tell us the exact GPU instance family for canary we’ll lock the kernel set.

I’ll cover the above in the kickoff; happy to dig into any of these items pre-meeting if needed.

—Marcus
Senior Applied ML Engineer — Redwood Inference

2) Quality prompts: I’ll send the 20 prompt samples by 10:30 AM PT.

Also, can you include a short checklist in the kickoff deck for the legal/compliance handoff (audit logs, retention policy, and a simple SOC2 evidence list)? Lina needs that for procurement sign-off.

Onwards — see you at 11.

Samir
